gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: The report highlighted the ___ of sport in schools (IMPORTANT).
gaps.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: importance (-ance).
After 'an important' a noun is needed: discovery (note the change from -er to -y).

gaps.sentence: Their ___ was celebrated with a big party (MARRY).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'Their'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'marry' is 'marriage' (-age); an adjective cannot follow 'Their' as subject.

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ until Thursday (SCHEDULE).
gaps.hint: arranged for a new time (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again/afresh: rescheduled means given a new time. The passive needs the past participle.

gaps.sentence: The magazine ___ the politician's words, which caused a scandal (QUOTE).
gaps.hint: quoted wrongly — that is why there was a scandal (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misquoted explains the scandal. The past tense is needed.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.
